premises: Tungsten addition to BCC refractory HEAs enhances high-temperature strength via solution strengthening and increased lattice distortion.
Tungsten-containing refractory HEAs retain a single-phase BCC structure and acceptable ductility at elevated temperatures.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase BCC dendritic structure with reported yield/compressive strengths of 330/423 MPa at 1273 K.
Tungsten addition improves thermal conductivity, aiding heat transfer between W and CuCrZr.
The proposed TiVNbTaW variant will not form brittle secondary phases that degrade ductility or thermal properties.
